subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dustin Lee <dustin.lee@apertureanalytics.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan & next steps

Dustin — great to meet yesterday. Quick recap and the MAP milestone we discussed (technical evaluation plan) so we can align on scope, success criteria, owners and target close. Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.pdf (MAP milestone & timeline) and tech-eval-plan.xlsx (detailed test matrix + infra assumptions).

High-level recap and ask
- Goal: Prove model candidate(s) meet your latency and cost thresholds while preserving answer quality on Aperture's customer prompts.
- Target close for MAP milestone: 2026-07-15 (agreed as part of commercial decision gate).

Technical evaluation plan (summary)
- Success criteria (benchmarks):
  - Latency: p95 end-to-end generation <= 150 ms on production-like traffic (target; see note)
  - Throughput: sustain 50 rps with <=200ms median latency
  - Cost: inference cost <= $0.02 / 1k tokens (target unit economics for production)
  - Quality: >= 90% of Aperture evaluation set rated acceptable on rubric (precision/accuracy + hallucination tolerance)
- Model shortlist (initial): Mistral-Instruct-7B, Llama2-Chat-13B (quantized), Falcon-7B-Instruct (baseline)
- Hardware targets: Dedicated H100 or equivalent for final validation; A100 test runs acceptable for early benchmarking
- Dataset: Aperture to provide 2–5k representative prompts + reference outputs. We'll augment with synthetic edge-cases.
- Timeline: 2 weeks of benchmark runs + 1 week for analysis and recommendation (3 weeks total)

Responsibilities (proposed)
- Aperture (you): share dataset, success-priority rubric, and any PII handling notes by 2026-06-17
- Redwood: provision bench infra, run evaluation scripts, and deliver a scorecard + recommendation by 2026-07-01
- Joint: review call to validate results and decide final model & quantization plan (target 2026-07-08)

Dependencies / Risks
- Access to representative prompts (blocking)
- Dataset size/format changes that require extra preprocessing
- If Aperture requires on-prem testing, timeline shifts by ~1 week for infra setup

Next steps
1) Confirm dataset sharing path and NDA scope (if required) — ACTION: Dustin (due 2026-06-17)
2) Redwood to provision bench and share evaluation script list — ACTION: Marissa / Dev (due 2026-06-12)
3) Kickoff technical eval once dataset is available (target start 2026-06-19)

Thanks — I attached the MAP draft and detailed tech plan. Please reply with any changes and confirm the dataset timeline.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.pdf (summary), tech-eval-plan.xlsx (test matrix)

Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation plan & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and aligns with our conversation. A few clarifications/questions before we confirm:

1) Latency target: you list p95 <= 150 ms as a target. Is that achievable on 13B models in your Dedicated offering, or is that only for H100-class hardware? Our production SLA target is strict and we want to understand what's realistic with quantized 13B vs 7B models.
2) Concurrent users / traffic shape: our expected peak is ~1k concurrent sessions (which maps to ~200 rps sustained with bursts). Will the bench simulate that load or do we need a separate stress run?
3) Baseline model: can you run one existing model we already use internally so we have a like-for-like comparison? (We can provide the baseline model name.)

We can share a first pass of the prompt set by 6/16. One ask: can you include estimated cost per 1k tokens for each model candidate (even if approximate)? That will help our finance folks.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation plan & next steps

Dustin — thanks for the quick review and excellent questions. Short answers below, and I updated the attached tech-eval-plan.xlsx with a stress-run section and provisional cost estimates (see the Cost tab).

1) Latency: p95 <= 150 ms is achievable on a quantized 13B on Dedicated H100 with careful batching and prefix caching. For A100/standard Dedicated configs we typically see p95 ~180–220 ms for 13B; 7B variants are easier to hit <150 ms. We'll include both 13B (quant) and 7B results in the report so you can choose the best trade-off for accuracy vs latency.

2) Traffic shape and stress runs: we will run two phases — functional benchmark (representative prompts at ~50 rps) and stress test (burst simulation up to 200–250 rps). If you want a full 1k concurrent session simulation, that will require a distributed load generator; we can include a scoped stress add-on (estimate in the sheet).

3) Baseline model: share the baseline model name and we will include it as an anchor.

Proposed minor MAP update based on your ask:
- Update success criteria to include a stress bucket: sustained 200 rps <= p95 250 ms (pass/fail)
- Redwood to include cost estimates per model candidate (approx $/1k tokens) in the scorecard

ACTION items updated in attached MAP-draft-v1.pdf
- Dustin: dataset + baseline model name by 2026-06-16
- Redwood: infra provisioned + evaluation scripts list by 2026-06-12 (done)
- Joint kick: target start 2026-06-19 (assuming dataset delivered)

I’ve forwarded this to Dev so he can confirm the bench infra config.

Best,
Marissa
